# Limit the number of power-up slots

**Headline:** Cap the run's permanent loadout at six slots shared across power-ups *and* weapons; the first six distinct kinds taken as permanent rewards define the run, and once all six slots are full only those kinds (plus flagged always-available entries such as Extra Life and Mystery UFO) may spawn or be offered as a new permanent pick. Field pickups never consume a slot.

## Original request (verbatim)

> Currently the player can collect any number of powerups. This makes them way too powerful in late game. Limit the number of power-ups that can be collected to 6. The first 6 collected permanently (i.e. from the hull-full) become the only powerups the player can collect in that game. Once the 6 slots are full with permanent items no other powerup kind will spawn (a life powerup is an exception, there may be other exceptions later in the development cycles, so availability when full should become a flag on the powerup database entry). Until all 6 slots are full powerups will spawn as they do now.

> **Terminology:** the item text says "hull-full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** (`MineralChoiceScene`, driven by the mineral hold — GDD §4.5). This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", i.e. a **permanent reward** grant. "Collected permanently" means a hold-full (or mini-boss reward) grant, never a field pickup.

## Problem statement

Players can currently collect every power-up and weapon kind in the catalogue, and every hold-full (permanent) reward can add a brand-new kind with no upper bound. By the late game a player therefore owns every permanent effect at once, which makes the ship far too powerful and flattens the difficulty curve. The run needs a bounded loadout: **six permanent slots shared across power-up and weapon kinds**. The first six distinct kinds the player takes as permanent rewards fill the slots; once all six are full, no other kind spawns or is offered as a new permanent pick, except kinds explicitly flagged as available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO today). Until the slots are full, spawning is unchanged.

## Users

- **Player (arcade run)** — wants a strong but bounded loadout, so late-game runs stay challenging and each run has a recognisable build identity; a drop on screen must still be worth catching.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the cap data-driven, with per-entry exemptions (Extra Life, Mystery UFO today; more later) needing no code change.
- **Agent / developer** — needs one shared implementation so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, once I have taken six permanent rewards my build is fixed for the rest of the run, so my late-game ship is strong but no longer invincible.
- As a player with six full slots, the only drops I see are the six kinds I chose (plus Extra Life and Mystery UFO), so every pickup improves something I own.
- As a designer, I can mark a catalogue entry as available-when-full, so a future exception is a data change, not a code change.
- As an operator, I can observe the identical slot rule in the gyms as in the shipped game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cap and shared accounting** — A single named, exported cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`) governs permanent ownership; occupied slots equal the count of **distinct drop kinds currently held** — power-up ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` / `permanentGrants()`) **or** an active temporary (field-pickup) stack (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks()`), plus weapon drop ids with a permanent level ≥ 1 (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`) **or** an active temporary weapon stack (`Player.getTempWeaponStacks()`), i.e. one shared pool of six (producer answers 2026-10-27: Q4 = a). A slot is released when the temporary window expires (`clearTemporary` / `tickWeaponTimers`). Entries flagged `availableWhenSlotsFull` never occupy a slot (Q7 = a). The permanent cannon and the `reset` utility are never counted (they cannot be permanently granted). A unit test proves the accounting: six distinct held grants fill the pool, a repeat grant of an owned kind levels it up without consuming a new slot, a temporary stack of a new kind consumes one, and the slot frees again when the temporary window expires. Exempt entries and `reset` never occupy a slot.2. **Spawn gating at full slots** — When all six slots (permanent **or** temporary — the union) are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six held kinds plus every catalogue id flagged available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO are flagged by default) and the slot-exempt `reset` utility; every other power-up *and weapon* id is never drawn. Verified by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper plus a `PlayScene` integration test that fills the slots and asserts a large sample of draws contains only held/exempt ids.3. **No behaviour change below the cap** — While fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change (power-ups and weapons alike).
4. **Choice gating at full slots** — Once the slots are full, a hold-full offer (and the mini-boss reward, which reuses the same option builder) offers **only items currently in the slots**: level-ups of permanently-owned kinds, base picks for kinds held only temporarily (taking one makes it permanent — it already occupies its slot), plus available-when-full entries (which never occupy a slot). A base entry that is neither held nor exempt is never offered, so a seventh kind can never be taken. Verified by choice-pool tests at 6 filled slots covering both power-up and weapon offers (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q6 = a, with the Q4 note: at full slots only offer items currently in the slots).5. **Data-driven exemption** — The exemption is a flag on the power-up catalogue entry (`availableWhenSlotsFull`, default `false`), not an `id === '…'` special case; Extra Life **and** Mystery UFO set it. A test asserts both are exempt, that every other catalogue entry defaults to non-exempt, and that a newly added entry is non-exempt unless it opts in. (No weapon exemption exists today; the flag stays power-up-only until a weapon needs one.)
6. **Parity and run scope** — The rule lives once in shared core code consumed by `PlayScene` and the formation gyms (guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / parity tests); slot state is run-scoped and resets on run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()` / `Player.resetWeaponLevels()`), and a temporary window's expiry also releases its slot. A parity/integration test proves the gym path and the game path consume the same gate.7. **Documentation and suite** — The GDD (§4.4 catalogue table and §4.5 hold-full choice) and `docs/BALANCING.md` document the shared six-slot cap and the exemption flag; the full project test suite passes with the change.

8. **Blocked collection at the cap with a distinct cue** — A drop whose kind is neither held, nor available-when-full, nor the slot-exempt `reset` utility is **not collectable** while the pool is full: on overlap it is not collected (no effect, no pickup cue, not removed), stays on the field, and plays a distinct **not-collectable SFX** — once per drop while it remains blocked — so the player can tell why the pickup failed (producer answer 2026-10-27: Q5 = b). When a slot frees (a temporary window expires) the same drop becomes collectable again. A test drives the shared collection seam at full slots and asserts: blocked drop kept, cue played exactly once, no effect/absorb applied; owned and exempt drops still collected; `reset` still collected; and the blocked drop is collectable after a slot frees.
## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1):** the rule must be implemented once in shared code (`src/powerups/*`, `src/scenes/core/*`) and consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms. A gym may only diverge for a documented, disabled-feature reason — none is expected here.
- **Single counter, derived from existing stores:** no new slot counter. Slot occupancy is derived from the two permanent-grant stores (`PowerUpLevelStore`, `Player._permanentWeaponGrants`), so existing level semantics stay the only source of truth.
- **Existing level semantics unchanged:** a repeat grant of an already-owned kind still levels it up (field pickup = temporary level, permanent reward = permanent level).
- **Determinism:** selection must stay injectable-rng deterministic; no wall-clock or `Math.random()` reads inside the new pure helpers.
- **No catalogue removals and no weight retuning:** the cap gates which ids may be drawn, not relative weights. `GameRules.powerUpWeights` / `weaponWeights` keep their meaning for the ids that remain eligible.
- **No individual rebalancing:** the six-slot cap is the balance change; per-item power tuning is out of scope.

## Existing state

- **"Power-up database":** `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry` / `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (16 power-ups); `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS` (power-ups) and `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS` (weapon drops) in `src/core/rules.ts`; `WEAPON_DROP_IDS`/`CHOICE_POOL` list weapon drops alongside.
- **Permanent ownership (power-ups):** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)`, `permanentGrants(id)`, `getLevels()` (permanent kinds only) and `getEffectiveLevel`/`getTempStacks` for temporary pickups.
- **Permanent ownership (weapons):** `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, `getPermanentWeaponLevel(id)`, `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent kinds only), `getTempWeaponStacks`; `resetWeaponLevels()` on run restart. The cannon can never be permanently granted (`isTimedWeapon` guard) and `reset` is not a `WeaponId`.
- **Game spawn path:** `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_maybeDropPowerUp()` rolls the level-resolved drop chance, then spawns `this.dropSpawner.next()`. The spawner is built once by `buildDefaultDropSpawner()` (`src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) as a `WeightedRandomSpawner<DropId>` over `POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS + WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, with weights from `src/core/rules.ts`. A small asteroid also rolls an additive deterministic `extra_life` drop.
- **Gym spawn paths:** `GymFormationScene._spawnPowerUpDrop()` (`powerUpSpawner`), `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeapons`, `GymLevel` — deterministic round-robin spawners.
- **Hold-full choice:** `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `buildChoiceCandidates()`, `drawWeightedWithoutReplacement()`, `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT`; `chooseOptions()` is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym, and the mini-boss reward reuses `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions()` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`).
- **Effects application:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect()` routes a collection to the power-up store's temporary stack or permanent grant; `Player.equipWeapon(…, permanent)` records weapon grants. No cap on distinct kinds exists today.
- **Docs of record:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (catalogue/table) and §4.5 (hold-full choice), `docs/BALANCING.md` (drop/choice balance), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention), `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Desired change

- Add `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` and an `availableWhenSlotsFull` flag on `PowerUpEntry` (Extra Life `true`, Mystery UFO `true`).
- Add a pure shared helper module (e.g. `src/powerups/slots.ts`) that, given the permanently-owned power-up ids, the permanently-owned weapon drop ids and the catalogues, answers: slots used, slots free, and whether a drop id may be drawn/offered. It owns the shared-pool and exemption rules — no `id === '…'` branches anywhere else.
- Apply that helper at the two decision points, both shared with the gyms:
  1. **drop selection** — the weighted draw excludes non-owned, non-exempt ids once the pool is full, for power-ups and weapons alike;
  2. **choice candidate construction** — `buildChoiceCandidates` excludes base entries that would create a seventh permanent kind once the pool is full, while owned level-up offers, exempt entries and the remaining candidates survive.
- Keep the below-cap path byte-for-byte equivalent in distribution (eligible set unchanged, weights unchanged).
- Cover with unit tests (helper + spawner + choice), integration tests (`PlayScene`), gym parity coverage, and documentation updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — add `availableWhenSlotsFull?: boolean` to `PowerUpEntry`; set `true` on `extra_life` and `mystery_ufo`; document default `false`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6` (mirroring existing `POWER_UP_*` constants).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` *(new)* + `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — pure shared-pool accounting and eligibility (power-ups + weapon drops, exemptions included).
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` — let a draw consult an eligibility predicate (or accept an eligible-id set) without weakening the all-zero-weight fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — a shared `drawNextDrop(spawner, slotState)` seam (built on `buildDefaultDropSpawner`) so every scene draws through one filtered path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the run's permanently-owned power-up and weapon ids into the drop draw (keep the asteroid `extra_life` path untouched).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — gate brand-new non-exempt kinds out of `buildChoiceCandidates` at the cap (owned level-ups and exempt entries remain).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` / `src/entities/Player.ts` — expose the owned-permanent-kind view consumed by the two gates (no new counter).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — consume the same filtered draw path (no divergent copy).
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` (new), `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (parity guard).
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 catalogue table + §4.5 choice), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `README.md` if it states power-up/weapon rules.

## Related work

- AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P — *As the levels progress increase the number of enemies and decrease the number of power ups* (level-resolved drop chance; the supply-side counterpart of this demand-side cap).
- AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X — *Add level-scaling module and tunable rules* (where `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1/Max` live; candidate home for a tunable cap).
- AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8 — *Smart Bomb is too powerful* (precedent for a single-item dominance fix; this item fixes dominance by accumulation instead).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 / AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR — power-up level curves and the `GymPowerUpLeveling` parity gym (the permanent-grant model this cap counts).
- AH-0MUTPEIZ5002FIJP — *P10 power-up identity — catalogue, spawn pool, choice pool and icon* (established that spawn pool and choice pool are catalogue-derived; the cap must not break that invariant).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention + duplicate-body guard.
- AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON — shared level-up option builder used by hold-full choice and mini-boss reward (the choice gate must be applied at the shared builder seam, not duplicated).
- AH-0MUCST4M7008O9CX — *Pluggable power-up choice strategy and permanent-effect support* (the `ChoiceStrategy` seam the choice gate extends).
- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — *Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling* (permanent weapon-grant semantics; weapons now share this item's slot pool).

## Risks and assumptions

- **All-zero-weight fallback:** `WeightedRandomSpawner` falls back to the first entry when every weight is zero, so exclusion must not be implemented by zeroing weights — it must be an eligibility filter applied before/while sampling.
- **Empty eligible set:** if all six owned kinds are currently unofferable and no exemption applies, the eligible set must never be empty; the draw must degrade to exempt/weapon entries rather than crash or always return one id.
- **Shared-pool starvation (design consequence):** because weapons share the six slots, a weapon-heavy build can consume the pool before any power-up reward is taken. This is the producer's chosen semantics (Q1 answer (c)); the docs must state it so it is not later mistaken for a bug. Balance evidence may need re-recording (out of scope).
- **Weapons granted by other permanent paths:** mini-boss unlocks/upgrades that set a permanent weapon level ≥ 1 also occupy a slot (derived from the same store); a document + test should pin that behaviour so the pool cannot be over-filled silently.
- **Test churn:** `src/core/rules.test.ts` and `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` assert the catalogue-complete pool; those assertions need an explicit "below cap" context.
- **Bot/balance evaluation drift:** `src/ai/eval/*` simulates campaigns and will see a different late-game loadout; re-recording bot evidence is *not* in scope unless a gate fails (record as a linked follow-up if needed).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD slot readout (`N/6`), persisting slots in checkpoints/saved runs, capping the mini-boss weapon unlock pool separately, and rebalancing individual power-up/weapon strength are out of scope; each becomes a linked work item rather than extra scope here.
- **Assumption (A1, resolved by Q1 answer (c)):** one shared pool of six across power-up and weapon kinds; field pickups excluded.
- **Assumption (A3):** no new player-facing HUD/UX surface is required by this item (producer did not request one; if wanted, it becomes an explicit AC or a linked item).
- **Assumption (A4):** the cap is a named code constant (default 6), not a persisted `GameRules` setting.
- **Assumption (A5):** the cap applies in the gyms as well as the game (parity); no gym is exempted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — What consumes a slot?** *Answer (producer):* **"c, field pickups are excluded"** — one shared pool of six across power-up *and* weapon kinds; temporary field-pickup stacks never consume a slot. **Resolved:** slots = distinct permanently-owned drop kinds (power-up permanent grants + weapon permanent levels), derived from the existing stores; no new counter. Source: interactive producer reply on AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.
- **Q2 — Does the hold-full choice also stop offering new kinds at the cap?** *Answer (producer):* **"a"** — yes, the choice is gated too: at six filled slots it offers level-ups of owned items and available-when-full entries only, never a new non-exempt kind (mini-boss reward inherits the same gate through the shared option builder). **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Q3 — Exemption flag and drops already on screen?** *Answer (producer):* **"a (Mystery UFO can also have the flag true)"** — the flag is `availableWhenSlotsFull` on the power-up catalogue entry (default `false`), set for **Extra Life and Mystery UFO**; drops of non-owned kinds already on screen when the sixth slot fills remain collectible for their temporary effect and simply stop spawning. **Resolved.** Source: interactive producer reply.
- **Assumption A3 (recorded, not contradicted):** no new HUD slot readout is required — if the producer wants an `N/6` indicator it becomes an explicit AC or a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A4 (recorded, not contradicted):** the cap ships as a named constant rather than a persisted `GameRules` field.
- **Assumption A5 (recorded, not contradicted):** gyms obey the same cap (parity).
- **Q4–Q7 (answered 2026-10-27 by producer, see blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM):** Q4(a) temporary pickups occupy a slot while held and free it on expiry, and a hold-full at full slots offers only items currently in the slots; Q5(b) block collection of a non-owned non-exempt drop at the cap with a distinct not-collectable SFX; Q6(a) the choice gate follows the union; Q7(a) exempt entries never occupy a slot.
- **Research note:** duplicate-work check performed (`wl search` on "powerup slots limit", "powerup cap", "power-up limit", "spawn pool", "hold-full choice pool", "too powerful", "power creep") — no item (open or completed) implements a permanent loadout cap, so this item is not a duplicate. Closest completed work is the level-scaled power-up *supply* reduction (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and the Smart Bomb power reduction (AH-0MV8GPGBL009M0D8); both are related, neither covers loadout breadth.

## Plan: decomposition (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (effort Small, risk Medium); the plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (approval is requested only for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was needed. The brief's own Appendix already carried producer answers Q1–Q3, so no new questions were required.

**Phasing (vertical slices, test-first).** Every phase is a test + implementation pair so each slice is reviewable end-to-end; the docs phase closes the item. Between phases the next item's description is re-read and updated against what actually shipped.

**Acceptance-criteria coverage** (manual traceability check — the parent ACs are a numbered list, which the automated `tree_coverage` extractor does not parse, so coverage was verified directly; Jaccard scores of the best-matching child AC: AC1 0.84 (item 1), AC2 0.97 (item 4), AC3 0.97 (item 3), AC4 0.98 (items 5/6), AC5 0.65 (item 1), AC6 0.98 (item 7), AC7 0.96 (item 8)):

No catalogue removal, no weight retuning and no per-item rebalancing are planned — the cap gates eligibility only, as the constraints require.

## Change of plan — 2026-10-25 producer audit (authoritative, supersedes parts of AC1–AC7)

The producer rejected the shipped implementation with this audit verdict (recorded
in the audit store, author `rgardler`, audited 2026-10-25T22:54:56Z):

> Rejected by manual review. Change of plan the slots should be limited to 6 slots
> for both permanent and temporary (field) pickups.

That verdict supersedes the earlier Q1 answer (c) ("field pickups excluded") and
the AC text that says field pickups never consume a slot. It is also **not** what
shipped in v0.1.15: `src/powerups/slots.ts` derives occupancy from the permanent
grants only, and the GDD §4.4 / `docs/BALANCING.md` say so explicitly. The delta
therefore has to be re-planned as a new increment on top of the eight closed
children (which stay closed).

### What the change touches

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — occupancy (`resolveSlotState`), eligibility
  (`isWithinSlotPool` / `eligibleDropIds`) and the "full" definition.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — the candidate gate at full slots.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` / `PlayScene.ts` + the gym
  scenes — the callers that resolve the slot state.
- Tests that pin the current semantics (`src/powerups/slots.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/slots.weaponLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`) and the
  docs assertions (`src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4/§4.5 and `docs/BALANCING.md`.

Temporary state is already exposed per kind (`PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacks(id)` /
`getEffectiveLevel(id)`, `Player.getTempWeaponStacks(id)` / `getWeaponLevel(id)`), so
a temporary-aware occupancy can still be **derived** (no new counter) for option (a)
of Q4 below.

### Resolved — producer answers 2026-10-27 (all four answered; recorded in the
blocking comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM)

- **Q4 → (a)** — a kind occupies a slot while held permanently **or** temporarily;
  the slot frees when the field-pickup window expires. Occupancy stays derived from
  the existing stores. With the answer came an explicit note: **if a hold-full is
  offered while all slots are full then only offer items that are currently in the
  slots** — this is AC4's gate.
- **Q5 → (b)** — a non-owned, non-exempt drop is blocked at the cap (a collection
  gate), and **there must be an SFX indicating it is not collectable** — this is
  AC8.
- **Q6 → (a)** — the choice gate follows the union: at full slots only items
  currently in the slots are offered (level-ups of permanent owned kinds, base
  picks for temp-held kinds, exempt entries).
- **Q7 → (a)** — exempt entries (`extra_life`, `mystery_ufo`) never occupy a slot;
  the flag exempts them from the count as well as from the spawn gate.

### Assumptions that stand unless contradicted

- A3 no HUD `N/6` readout; A4 the cap stays the named constant `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`;
  A5 the gyms obey the same rule; the permanent cannon and the `reset` utility never
  count; a repeat pickup of an already-slotted kind levels that slot and never adds a
  second one.
- Existing docs/tests asserting "field pickups never consume a slot" are **rewritten**,
  not deleted, once the decisions land.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25 — plan skill: created 8 child items (4 test-first items before their implementation pairs, plus parity evidence and docs), wired 9 dependency edges, verified AC coverage, advanced stage to `plan_complete`. No existing content removed; producer answers Q1–Q3 and assumptions A3–A5 carried forward unchanged.

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want an executable contract (failing tests) for the two level-scaling axes before any production code exists, so the curves, rounding rules and cap behaviour are pinned before implementation.

This is the test-first item for the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` module and the `GameRules` scaling data (AC "Data-driven level-scaling curves" and the unit-test part of AC "Tests" of the parent item AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

## What to do

Create `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts` (new file) and extend `src/core/rules.test.ts` with tests that pin the agreed contract. These tests must **fail on pre-change HEAD** because neither the module nor the rules fields exist yet.

Curve contract to pin:

# We need an outer loop (AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC)

## Objective

**User story (producer).** As the producer, I want the region/home-world proposal
plus **two genuinely different** outer-loop candidates, each written up as a
decision-ready outline on the same footing, so that I can choose one and have it
written into the Game Design Document (GDD) with confidence.

**User story (player).** As a player, I want something to carry forward between
runs — a long-term goal and a sense that my play changes the world — so that
losing a run does not mean losing all progress, and so that beating the final
boss is a milestone on the way to winning rather than the end of everything.

## Users

- **Producer / designer (primary).** Chooses one of three outlined loops and owns
  the GDD write-up; needs comparable, honest outlines and a defensible ranking.
- **Player (arcade / bullet-hell fan).** Needs a reason to return after a lost
  run and a goal beyond a high score; wants progress that survives failure.
- **Developer / agent implementing the loop later.** Needs each outline to name
  the systems, seams and gym coverage so the chosen loop can be planned without
  re-deriving the design.

## Problem statement

The game has a strong **inner loop** (flying, dodging formations, destroying
enemies) and a functioning **middle loop** (per-run ship upgrading through
minerals → hold-full power-up choices → levelled weapons), but **no outer loop**:
nothing persists between runs except a leaderboard score, player settings and a
single run checkpoint. A death ends the run outright (GDD §4.6: "There is no
continue mechanic. Game over is final"), so long-term engagement rests entirely
on score chasing. The fiction ("pilot a resistance ship through a digital
underworld ruled by rogue AI") implies a war to be won, but the game currently
has no structure that represents winning it.

The producer has proposed one candidate outer loop (contested regions with a
home world to find and defend) and asked for **two other candidates** to be
brainstormed and outlined, after which the producer chooses one for the GDD.

## Deliverable

A single design-exploration document — `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — built
to the same standard as the existing research catalogues
(`docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`):
selected candidates written up per-concept, a "considered but not selected"
section, and a selection recommendation. It is a **design document only**: no
gameplay code, no persistence schema changes and no new scenes are implemented
in this item.

The producer's choice is then written into the GDD as a follow-on work item; this
item ends at the candidate document, the comparison and the recommendation.

## Loop tiers used by the document

| Tier | Timescale | Definition in this game | Exists today? |
|------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------|
| **Inner** | Seconds | Flying, dodging, destroying enemies and formations within a wave | Yes (GDD §2.3–2.6) |
| **Middle** | Minutes (a run) | Ship upgrading: minerals → hold-full power-up/weapon choices, levelled effects, extra lives | Yes (GDD §4.4, §4.6) |
| **Outer** | Hours (a campaign / a season) | What the player carries **between** runs and what they are ultimately trying to achieve | **No** |

## Candidate A — Contested Regions / Home World (producer's proposal)

Recorded as proposed, not redesigned. Its outline must preserve every named
mechanic:

- Space is divided into **regions**; each region has an **AI aggression level**.
- The ship can **warp a limited distance** to adjacent regions.
- The goal is to find a region with **zero aggression** containing a **planet
  that can become home to the humans**.
- Having found it, the player must **defend all adjacent regions** against
  attack by aggressive AI.
- The player may leave their **fully upgraded ship** in a region with an **AI
  automated pilot** that defends that region.
- The player then returns home and **collects another ship with no upgrades**,
  and must go out again to make it strong enough to be left guarding another
  region.
- **Factional AI warfare** changes region strength over time: warring AI
  factions fight over a region and the winner leaves a stronger force there.
- **Win condition:** all regions have successfully defended against a massive AI
  onslaught, at which point the home world is safe and the game is won.

The outline must state its **minimal first slice** (the smallest version that
proves the loop is fun), because the full proposal is the largest of the three.

## Candidate B — Salvage Fleet (proposed direction, resource-persistent meta)

A **roguelite meta-progression** outer loop that leaves the map alone and
persists **player power** instead.

- Between runs the player spends **banked salvage** (minerals and mini-boss AI
  cores extracted at the existing checkpoint moments) in a persistent **hangar**
  to unlock hulls, starting weapons and permanent modifiers.
- Each run is a **deployment** flown in one chosen hull; losing the run forfeits
  that run's unbanked salvage but never the hangar.
- The outer goal is to assemble a fleet strong enough for a final assault run at
  maximum threat.
- Progression axis: **build/economy** (what the player owns), not territory.

## Candidate C — Signal Decode (proposed direction, knowledge-persistent meta)

A **campaign-mutating** outer loop where the thing that persists is
**information**.

- Mini-bosses and the boss drop **data fragments** that assemble a persistent
  codex revealing the origin of the AI and the "hellscape" it generates.
- Codex knowledge **mutates and unlocks the campaign** (new enemy behaviours,
  hellscape modifiers, shortcuts), and the final confrontation only becomes
  winnable once the core's rules have been decoded — the boss's phases are the
  codex's payoff.
- Progression axis: **knowledge and campaign variation**, not territory or
  currency.

## Required outline structure (every candidate)

1. **Fantasy / pitch** — one paragraph, in the game's fiction.
2. **Loop structure** — moment-to-moment → run → meta, with an explicit
   statement of *what carries between runs*.
3. **States** — win, lose, partial progress and what a bad run still advances.
4. **New systems** required (named, with rough size).
5. **Reuse of existing systems** — checkpoint (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`),
   minerals/power-up levels, `Leaderboard`, difficulty curves
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`), mini-boss rewards, bot/attract mode.
6. **Persistence and save model** — a sketch `localStorage` payload under
   §6.6 rules (defensive parse, no backend) with migration note.
7. **Session shape** — target run length and hours-to-win.
8. **UI / scene surface** — which new screens or menu entries are needed.
9. **Gym testability and the bot** — how its gameplay additions can be exercised
   in a gym (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity rule) and how attract mode can complete
   or avoid stalling on the outer loop.
10. **Pillar impact** — which current GDD pillars it changes (e.g. "no continue,
    game over is final", the single final boss), stated explicitly.
11. **Effort and risk** — sized honestly, with the failure modes that would make
    the loop unfun.
12. **Minimal first slice** — the smallest shippable version.

A **comparison table** then ranks all candidates on: fit with the existing
pilots-in-a-digital-hell fiction, reuse of shipped systems, new-system cost,
persistence complexity, session length fit, legibility of progress to the player,
gym/bot testability, and risk of trivialising or gutting the shipped campaign —
followed by an explicit **recommendation with rationale** and why the others rank
lower. A "Considered but not selected" section records further ideas (e.g. an
arcade-style tiered mutator ladder, a pure daily-seed challenge ladder) with a
one-line deferral reason each.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Deliverable exists and frames the problem.** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
   exists, opens with the inner/middle/outer tier definitions above and the
   comparison criteria, and states that it is design-only.
2. **Candidate A is complete and faithful.** Candidate A is written up with all
   twelve required sections and preserves every mechanic listed in *Candidate A*
   above (regions, limited warp, per-region aggression, zero-aggression home
   region with a habitable planet, defence of adjacent regions, autonomous-pilot
   ship hand-off, unupgraded replacement ship, faction warfare, all-regions-held
   win). No proposed mechanic is silently dropped, altered or merged.
3. **Two additional candidates, materially distinct.** Candidates B and C each
   carry all twelve required sections and each names *what persists between
   runs* differently from Candidate A and from each other; each is justified
   against at least one named design pillar or fiction element.
4. **Decision-ready comparison.** The document contains a comparison table across
   the agreed criteria, an explicit recommendation with rationale, and a ranked
   justification for why the two non-recommended candidates rank lower.
5. **Alternatives recorded.** A "Considered but not selected" section lists at
   least two further outer-loop ideas with a one-line deferral reason each.
6. **Docs guard test.** A vitest docs-guard test (convention:
   `src/classicPowerUpWeaponResearchDocs.test.ts`) asserts the document exists,
   contains the tier definitions, the comparison table and, for each of the three
   candidates, the twelve required section headings — so the deliverable cannot
   silently regress. It passes in the changed-scope test gate.
7. **Cross-linked, not orphaned.** The new document is cross-linked from the GDD
   future-scope section (§8) and from where the other design catalogues are
   referenced in `README.md`; every added link resolves to a file or anchor that
   exists.

# Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable

## Problem statement

The improved Phase Shift / wormhole-emergence treatment shipped under
AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S (commits 4267a534, 4b407b66, eafc45b6, c84c1a99, 5b5877e4) is
technically complete and audited, but **the producer reports it is still not
noticeable enough — the effect must be unmistakable**. The intent of the original
epic ("instantly obvious that they are not in their usual state") is therefore not
yet satisfied in practice, even though every written acceptance criterion passed.

Producer feedback (2026-10-25, verbatim): *"These effects are not noticeable
enough, needs to be unmistakable."*

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, the instant my ship phases out — or enemies
  start materialising out of the wormhole — I want to *know* without looking for
  it. Not a tint I have to hunt for: an unmistakable event."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I
  want the activation to read like a system event (a hit, a pulse, a distortion),
  not a subtle colour shift, so I can trust it and time my flying."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want whatever stronger treatment we
  choose to live once in the shared VFX layer, stay toggleable per layer, and keep
  the gyms and the game pixel-identical."

## Current state (what shipped, and why it reads as subtle)

Screen-wide Phase Shift (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`):

| Layer | Current value |
|---|---|
| Dim overlay | dark blue 0x0a1a33, alpha 0.22 |
| Chromatic split | cyan 0x33ffee / red 0xff3355, **alpha 0.20**, base offset **6 px** (+/-1.5 px, 1.6 s) |
| Alpha flicker | 3 Hz, 25 % depth |
| Colour pulse | 0.75 -> 1.0 cross-fade |
| Activation burst | alpha 0.35 at +/-12 px, 200 ms fade |
| Camera shake | **deliberately none** (producer decision: it read like death juice) |

Per-enemy emergence (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` `updateEnemyShimmer`):
ripple burst +0.06 scale / +0.15 alpha over 200 ms, then alpha flicker 0.55-0.85 at
3 Hz, scale pulse 4 %, additive-bloom colour pulse (Phaser 4 `Container`/`Graphics`
have no Tint).

Wormhole ring (`attachWormholeRing`): 0xd9b3ff, r 52 px, 3 px stroke, alpha 0.45,
yoyo scale 0.9-1.15 every 900 ms.

Diagnosis of the shortfall (to be confirmed with the producer): every layer is a
**low-alpha translucent tint at screen-wide scale**, and translucency over a busy
bullet-hell background is perceptually weak. "Unmistakable" most likely needs
*high-contrast, structural* change — distortion, a hard flash, silhouettes, motion —
not just larger alpha values.

## Candidate approaches (producer to choose / amend)

**A — Bigger same-technique (lowest risk, no new rendering technique).**
Split alpha 0.20 -> ~0.45 and offset 6 -> ~14 px; burst alpha 0.35 -> ~0.70 at
+/-28 px over ~320 ms; add a short full-screen brightness flash on activation
(distinct palette from the death flash); add cyan edge/vignette bands during phase
(the defeat-screen vignette technique) so the *frame* changes, not just the objects;
per-enemy alpha flicker range widened (e.g. 0.25-1.0) plus a stroked silhouette
outline per emerging enemy; wormhole ring radius/alpha raised with an open shockwave.

**B — Real screen-space distortion via Phaser camera post-FX (highest impact).**
Use the engine's built-in post-FX pipelines on the main camera while phased: a
short displacement/pixelate wobble on the activation edge, then a sustained subtle
`Bloom`/`Glow` + gentle `Barrel`/`Displacement` wobble, all driven from the same
tunables. This is the genuine "glitch" read and is far more visible than alpha
tints. Caveats: the original epic explicitly scoped shader/render-to-texture work
out; needs a WebGL check + a headless-safe fallback, a measurable perf check, and a
canvas-renderer degradation path. Phaser post-FX state must also be torn down
exactly on the falling edge.

**C — Combination (recommended by the agent, producer decides).**
A for the player + wormhole (cheap, robust) **plus** B's activation-edge distortion
burst only (a ~150-250 ms pixelate/displacement hit), so the *event* is unmistakable
while the *sustained* state stays comfortable.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge.
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer.
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing.
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay.
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes.
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe.
- Tests and docs: unit tests cover every new layer, teardown, fallback and the no-shake regression; GDD section 7.2 and code comments document all tunables; the full suite passes.

## Acceptance notes (detail per criterion)

1. **Activation edge (aggressive).** Rising edge fires, in the same frame: a ~150-250 ms camera-filter distortion burst (pixelate + barrel/displacement wobble), a full-screen flash in a phase-shift palette (never the player-death flash palette), and the widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair. Every magnitude is an exported tunable; every layer has its own `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle.
2. **Sustained state (soft).** Split alpha/offset raised and slowly oscillating, cyan edge/vignette band layer, gentle sustained filter layer; sustained flicker capped at <=3-4 Hz for seizure safety; no camera shake.
3. **Teardown detail.** A second expiry, a scene `SHUTDOWN` or a re-activation cycle leaves no residual tint, no leaked filter controller, no duplicated layer; pre-existing unrelated camera filters survive untouched.
4. **Fallback detail.** Renderer probe checks the WebGL renderer type and the camera filter list; unsupported renderers get the overlay-only layers with no error storm (headless/canvas tests exercise this path).
5. **Emergence detail.** Driven from the shared spawn path (`updateSpawnAnimation` -> `updateEnemyShimmer`) over the whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`; the entity's own alpha/scale/blend state is fully restored when growth ends.
6. **Wormhole detail.** One ring and one shockwave per wormhole; tweens stopped before destroy; registry cleared on close.
7. **Distinctness detail.** The no-shake regression test is retained; the duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion stay green.
8. **Docs detail.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 plus JSDoc on every new exported constant and helper.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)

- **Q1 = C** — combination: approach A (bigger same-technique + frame-level flash/vignette/silhouette) everywhere, **plus** approach B's screen-space distortion for the player path.
- **Q2 = iii** — aggressive on the activation edge, soft for the sustained state.
- **Q3 = no shake** — the no-camera-shake decision stands; the "punch" comes from post-FX/flash layers only. The existing regression test stays.
- **Q4 = ship and iterate** — the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S is **not** held: no dependency edge from the epic to this item; it releases through the normal dev->main gate and this item improves the effect afterwards.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which approach?** (A) bigger same-technique only; (B) real screen-space post-FX distortion for the player path; (C) combination.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **C**. Rationale: keep the robust overlay/vignette/silhouette work everywhere and add a genuine distortion read for the player's activation.
- **Q2 — How far may intensity go?** (i) comfortably strong; (ii) aggressive/startling; (iii) aggressive activation edge, soft sustained.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **iii**. Rationale: the *event* must be unmistakable; the *state* must stay comfortable for the whole phase duration.
- **Q3 — Revisit the no-shake rule?** (i) keep no-shake, use post-FX/flash instead; (ii) allow a short low-intensity shake on the activation edge only.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **no shake**. Rationale: preserves the established distinctness from player-death juice.
- **Q4 — Release hold for the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S?** hold its release until this lands, or ship and iterate.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **ship and iterate**. No blocking edge is wired from the epic to this item.

## Technical feasibility note (verified before planning)

Phaser 4.2.1 exposes camera filters (`camera.filters.internal` / `.external`):
`addPixelate`, `addBarrel`, `addGlow`, `addVignette`, `addBlur`, `addParallelFilters`
(bloom), `addDisplacement`, `addColorMatrix`. They are **WebGL only**, so the driver
must probe `scene.game.renderer.type` / `camera.filters` and degrade to the
overlay-only layers otherwise. No post-FX is used anywhere in `src/` today, so this is
a new (but engine-supported) technique.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — finalise after producer answers Q1-Q3)

- **Unmistakable activation read (player).** On the `isPhased` rising edge the
  treatment produces a structural, high-contrast change (not merely a tint): the
  chosen mechanism (A/B/C) fires within the same frame and is perceptible against a
  busy background in a manual play check; magnitudes exported as tunables with
  per-layer toggles.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player).** While phased, the state remains
  continuously obvious for the whole duration (chosen sustained layer(s) from A
  and/or B), with the no-camera-shake guarantee intact and every layer torn down on
  the falling edge (no residual tint or residual post-FX state).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies).** Each emerging enemy is individually
  obvious as "not solid yet" across its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` window, driven
  from the shared spawn path; the entity's own render state is fully restored when
  growth ends; no screen-wide overlay on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is clearly the source of the emergence (ring
  and/or column strengthened per the chosen approach), tracked in the existing
  `wormholeEffects` registry and fully cleared on close.
- **No regressions.** Death juice stays visually distinct; the no-shake regression
  holds (unless the producer reverses it, in which case it is updated deliberately);
  gym<->game parity guards pass; headless no-op tests pass.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the new
  layers/mechanism creation + teardown (including post-FX teardown if chosen), and
  the no-shake and headless guarantees. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2
  and the code comments are updated with the final magnitudes. The full project test
  suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — magnitudes, new layers, optional
  camera post-FX driver.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — per-enemy treatment, wormhole ring.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (post-FX needs a camera).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared helpers only (no new behaviour).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 — final treatment + tunables.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (completed, audited, awaiting release) — the epic that
  delivered the current treatment. This item is `discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S`.
  The producer must decide whether the epic's release is held until this lands.
- AH-0MVD2MXAB004K0V4 — player phase-shift juice (vivid split + burst + shimmer).
- AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9 — per-enemy emergence shimmer.
- AH-0MVD2N6AW0073X5M — wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS — original Phase Shift juice module (dim + split, no shake).
- AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB — end-of-run juice; the defeat glitch-flicker + vignette
  technique is the precedent for approach A's frame-level layers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: seizure sensitivity / discomfort** — "unmistakable" pushes toward higher
  contrast and faster flicker. Mitigation: cap sustained flicker, keep the aggressive
  part on the short activation edge, keep per-layer toggles, and track a
  reduce-motion accessibility option separately.
- **Risk: post-FX complexity and platform variance** (approach B) — WebGL-only,
  needs canvas fallback, exact teardown, and a perf measurement. Mitigation: fall
  back to approach A layers when post-FX is unavailable.
- **Risk: parity drift** — mitigated by implementing once in the shared VFX layer;
  guards enforce it.
- **Assumption:** the producer's "unmistakable" means *perceptually unavoidable*,
  not necessarily *physically larger* — the chosen mechanism is a producer decision
  (Q1-Q3 above).

# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction. Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).

## Summary

Implements the producer's 2026-10-27 change of plan for AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF: the six-slot cap must count **permanent and temporary (field) pickups alike**, a drop that cannot be taken at the cap must be **blocked with a distinct not-collectable SFX**, and a hold-full offer at full slots may only offer items **currently in the slots**.

Producer answers (recorded on the parent, comment AH-C0MVRC08UJ009D0CM):

- **Q4 → (a):** a kind occupies a slot while held permanently **or** temporarily; the slot frees when the field-pickup window expires. Plus the note: *"if a hold-full is offered while all slots are full then only offer items that are currently in the slots"*.
- **Q5 → (b):** block collection of a non-owned, non-exempt kind at the cap, **with an SFX indicating it is not collectable**.
- **Q6 → (a):** the choice gate follows the union of held kinds.
- **Q7 → (a):** `availableWhenSlotsFull` entries never occupy a slot.

Today (shipped v0.1.15) `src/powerups/slots.ts` derives occupancy from the **permanent** stores only, and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 states "Field pickups never consume a slot". This item changes that rule in one place and re-points every consumer.

## User stories

- As a player, I can never hold more than six distinct power-up/weapon kinds at once, whether I took them from the hold-full choice or picked them up on the field, so the late-game ship stays bounded.
- As a player, when a drop is visible but cannot be taken because my six slots are full, I hear a distinct "not collectable" cue instead of silently failing, and the drop stays on the field in case a slot frees.
- As a player, when my slots are full the hold-full choice only offers things I already hold (or the always-available exceptions), so I never waste a reward.
- As a designer, `availableWhenSlotsFull` remains the only exemption switch, and an exempt entry never consumes a slot.

## Deliverables

### 1. Union slot accounting (`src/powerups/slots.ts`, `powerUpLevels.ts`, `Player.ts`)

- `resolveSlotState(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels, tempPowerUpIds?, tempWeaponIds?)` — occupied slots = distinct drop kinds with a permanent level ≥ 1 **or** an active temporary stack. Defaulted optional parameters keep existing callers/tests compiling; temp ids are additive.
- `PowerUpLevelStore.getTempStacksSnapshot()` (or equivalent `getHeldTempIds()`) and `Player.getTempWeaponIds()` expose the temporary-held kinds (the store keeps `_tempStacks` / `_tempWeaponStacks` private today).
- `SlotPlayerView` gains the temp accessors; `resolvePlayerSlotState` passes them, so `PlayScene` and every gym derive occupancy identically.
- Exempt entries (`availableWhenSlotsFull === true`) and the slot-exempt `reset` utility never occupy a slot; `reset` is also never gated by the cap (it cannot be permanently granted). Keep the cannon excluded by construction.
- Update the module docs: union semantics, slot released on window expiry, exempt entries never occupy a slot, blocked collection is the caller's gate.

### 2. Blocked collection + not-collectable cue (`dropLayer.ts`, `CombatCoreScene.ts`, audio)

- `collectOverlappingDrops(drops, player, onCollect, dropSize?, options?)` gains an optional `{ canCollect?: (drop) => boolean; onBlocked?: (drop) => void }` seam: an ineligible drop is **kept on the field** and `onBlocked` fires instead of `onCollect`.
- `CombatCoreScene._collectOverlappingDrops` supplies the gate from `isWithinSlotPool(drop.dropId, _resolveDropSlotState())` and plays the new cue once per drop (a boolean flag on `CombatDrop`, e.g. `blockedCuePlayed`), so a drop overlapping for many frames does not spam audio. No effect, no absorb animation and no pickup cue run for a blocked drop.
- New SFX: recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-pickup-blocked.yaml`, manifest entry with a seed in the `32100-32199` block, render via `scripts/build-audio.sh --render` (ToneForge CLI is on PATH), `playPowerUpBlockedSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, and the mapping row in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`. The cue-manifest contract suite must stay green.

### 3. Choice gating on the held set (`choice.ts` + launchers)

- `ChoiceContext` gains `tempPowerUpIds?` / `tempWeaponIds?`; `buildChoiceCandidates` resolves the union slot state and, when full, keeps base entries only for kinds already held (so a temp-held kind can be made permanent — it already owns its slot) plus exempt entries. Level-up offers for permanently-owned kinds are unchanged.
- Every launcher that builds a `ChoiceContext` passes the temp ids: `PlayScene` (4 sites), `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`.

### 4. Docs and guards

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (rewrite the "Field pickups never consume a slot" bullet into the union rule, the slot-release-on-expiry behaviour, exempt entries never occupying a slot, and the blocked-collection + cue behaviour) and §4.5 (choice offers only slotted items + exempt at full).
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the cap now bounds simultaneously-held breadth, including field pickups; record the churn consequence (slots free on expiry) as chosen semantics.
- `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts` — retarget the assertions to the new documented rule (rewrite, do not delete).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Union accounting** — occupied slots equal the number of distinct drop kinds held permanently **or** temporarily (power-up and weapon families share the pool); a temporary stack of a new kind consumes one slot, a repeat pickup of a held kind does not, and the slot is released when the temporary window expires (`clearTemporary` / `tickWeaponTimers`). `availableWhenSlotsFull` entries and `reset` never occupy a slot; the cannon is never counted. Unit tests cover power-up and weapon temp stacks, expiry release, exempt-entry exclusion, and six-into-full accounting.
2. **Spawn gating on the union** — at six held kinds (any mix) the shared draw returns only held kinds, exempt entries and `reset`; below the cap the draw sequence is unchanged for a fixed seed (existing regression test stays green).
3. **Blocked collection with a distinct cue** — at full slots a non-owned, non-exempt drop is not collected (kept on the field, no effect/absorb/pickup cue) and the new not-collectable cue plays exactly once per drop while it stays blocked; held, exempt and `reset` drops are still collected; the blocked drop becomes collectable again once a slot frees. Verified at the shared collection seam (`dropLayer`/`CombatCoreScene`) with an injected-cue spy.
4. **Choice gating** — at full slots a hold-full offer contains only level-ups of permanently-owned kinds, base picks for temp-held kinds and exempt entries; never a new non-exempt kind. Below the cap the candidate list is distributionally unchanged.
5. **Parity and run scope** — the rule lives once in `src/powerups/slots.ts`; `PlayScene` and every gym consume it (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the parity tests stay green); run restart (`PowerUpLevelStore.reset()` / `Player.resetWeaponLevels()`) clears both components so the pool is empty again.
6. **Docs and suite** — GDD §4.4/§4.5 and `docs/BALANCING.md` describe the union rule, the slot release on expiry, exempt entries never occupying a slot, and the blocked-collection cue; the docs assertion test is retargeted (not weakened); `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the changed-scope test gate passes.
7. **SFX asset pipeline** — the new cue has a ToneForge recipe, a manifest entry with a seed in the documented block, a rendered baked WAV plus checksum via `scripts/build-audio.sh --render`, an `effects.ts` export, and a `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` row; the cue-manifest contract test passes.

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF (the eight original children are closed; this is a new increment on top of the shipped permanent-only rule).
- Related: AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 (gym↔game parity guard), AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (temporary-vs-permanent split), AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J / AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD (ToneForge baked-audio pipeline).

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — union occupancy, slot-exempt ids (`reset`), eligibility docs.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — temporary-stack snapshot accessor.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getTempWeaponIds()` (+ the `SlotPlayerView` accessors).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceContext.tempPowerUpIds` / `tempWeaponIds`, held-set candidate gate.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — `collectOverlappingDrops` collection-gate seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — blocked-collection gate + once-per-drop cue; `CombatDrop.blockedCuePlayed`.
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-pickup-blocked.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `public/audio/sfx/` (rendered) — the not-collectable cue.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — pass temp ids into the choice context.
- Tests: `src/powerups/slots.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.weaponLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4, §4.5), `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the Force Field bubble/spent-dim behaviour and the new reflect cue documented in the design and audio references, and the whole repository suite proven green, so the change is auditable and safe to release.

## Scope

1. **GDD power-up row** — `docs/Game Design Document.md` line ~880, `force_field` row: state that the bubble persists while the field is active (including the permanent hold-full field), that it **dims** when the reflect budget is spent (never vanishes), and that each reflected bullet flashes at the bounce point with a dedicated cue (`playForceFieldReflectSound`). UK English, consistent table style.
2. **Audio reference** — `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`: confirm the cue row/seed/tier added by the intercept-feedback sibling is complete and consistent (fix gaps if any; do not duplicate the row).

5. **Full-suite verification** — run the repository test workflow through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`), never ad-hoc test commands, and triage any failure into a critical `test-failure` item per the triage policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC11 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC8 — Test coverage:** at least one unit test per changed seam exists and is green — bubble persistence (AC1), spent-dim rendering (AC2), the reflect-feedback seam (flash + cue once per intercept), the manifest/cue-coverage contract, and the shared constants (verified by reading the diffs and the suite result).
- The verification is performed *after* both implementation slices land; failures are either fixed here (trivial) or filed as blocking critical `test-failure` items (never silently waived).
